articles.title: Emiratos Árabes Unidos avisa al Reino Unido de reducir su inversión en el país en función de lo severa que sea la sanción al City
articles.standfirst: Las relaciones entre ambos países son muy estrechas
articles.summary: Las relaciones entre ambos países son muy estrechas
articles.body: El Gobierno de Emiratos Árabes Unidos ha advertido con reducir la inversión en el Reino Unido en función de lo severa que sea la sanción que reciba el Manchester City en relación al caso de las irregularidades financieras del que fue declarado culpable esta semana por una comisión independiente de la Premier League. Según el medio económico Bloomberg, mandatarios de Emiratos Árabes Unidos han advertido al Gobierno británico de que la sanción que la comisión independiente decida y que puede ir desde la multa económica hasta la pérdida de puntos, descenso o incluso expulsión del fútbol profesional, puede tener un impacto en el "apetito para inversiones y compromisos a gran escala en el Reino Unido". El Manchester City fue comprado en 2008 por el fondo de inversión de Abu Dhabi, que desde entonces se ha encargado de inyectar dinero en el club. Tal y como ha sido demostrado por la Premier League, el conjunto inglés defraudó más de 1000 millones de euros entre 2009 y 2018 en patrocinios inflados, la mayoría de ellos con empresas procedentes de Emiratos Árabes Unidos. Según datos de Bloomberg, en los últimos cinco años, Emiratos Árabes Unidos ha invertido más de 30 mil millones de libras (36.000 millones de euros) en sectores importantes del Reino Unido como defensa, ciencia y tecnología, además de que hay planeada una cumbre entre los dos países para octubre. A su vez, la misma fuente indica que miembros del Gobierno británico están "frustrados" por la actitud de Emiratos Árabes Unidos en este escándalo, ya que entienden que estaban al tanto de las irregularidades cometidas por el Manchester City durante casi una década y que insistieron en que no estaban haciendo nada incorrecto. La posición de Emiratos Árabes Unidos llega después de las controvertidas palabras del primer ministro británico, Andy Burnham, que tuvo que retractarse tras decir que sería "muy preocupante" perder a los dueños del Manchester City si estos tuvieran que abandonar el club por el escándalo. Un portavoz de Downing Street tuvo que emitir un comunicado unas horas después en el que dejó claro que nadie está por encima de la ley y que los culpables tendrán que asumir las consecuencias de sus actos. El Manchester City comunicó este viernes que ya ha presentado la apelación por las irregularidades financieras. Se espera que haya un veredicto final para enero.

articles.title: 'Ignorant of the rules': Why Portugal and Jorge Jesus should not be blamed for making Rafael Leão wear Cristiano Ronaldo’s No. 7
articles.summary: Discover why Rafael Leão was assigned Cristiano Ronaldo's iconic No. 7 shirt after the star's departure from Portugal's camp. Learn how UEFA's squad-list regulations dictate jersey assignments and the public's reaction to this unexpected change.
articles.body: Cristiano Ronaldo had barely left Portugal's camp when Rafael Leão was already wearing his famous No. 7 shirt. Within hours, social media was filled with claims that Portugal had stripped Ronaldo of his number, that his replacement had already been chosen and that the federation was rushing to erase the CR7 era. It looked startlingly quick. But the reality is rather different, because Portugal had no option to leave the shirt vacant.Why Rafael Leão was suddenly wearing No. 7The change came after Ronaldo left Portugal's training camp on Wednesday following his disagreement with new manager Jorge Jesus.Ronaldo was due to miss Portugal's Nations League meeting with Denmark after leaving the squad, and UEFA's squad-list rules meant that Portugal could not simply leave his No. 7 unassigned.That is why Rafael Leão appeared in the famous shirt when Portugal faced Denmark at Parken Stadium on ThursdayLeão normally wears No. 17 for Portugal, but with Ronaldo no longer part of the matchday squad, the No. 7 had to be allocated to another player. Leão was moved into it, while his No. 17 was handed to new call-up Fábio Silva.The change immediately created a much bigger conversation than a simple squad-number adjustment.Images of Leão wearing Ronaldo's number spread rapidly across all social media, with many fans reacting as though Portugal had deliberately taken the shirt away from Ronaldo less than 24 hours after his departure.Some posts described the timing as disrespectful, arguing that the number had barely been vacated before another player was wearing it. Piers Morgan also criticised the decision on X, calling it “disgusting”, while other viral posts used the phrase that Ronaldo's “body is still warm” to express their anger at the speed of the change.Others directed their frustration towards Jesus, interpreting the decision as evidence of a personal vendetta against Ronaldo and suggesting that giving Leão the shirt was intended to signal the end of the CR7 era.Leão himself was also targeted by some Ronaldo supporters, who accused him of trying to take over the legacy attached to the number.The problem with that interpretation is that the shirt was not handed over as a symbolic declaration that Leão had replaced Ronaldo. Portugal was required to fill the number.UEFA's squad rules left Portugal with no way to keep No. 7 emptyThe explanation is buried in the way international squads are registered.Under Article 37 of the UEFA Nations League regulations, a 23-player matchday squad must use consecutive numbers from 1 through 23, with no gaps in the list.So when Ronaldo left the squad and No. 7 became available, Portugal could not simply leave it untouched as a tribute to him. The number still had to appear on the squad list. It also explains the knock-on change involving Leão. Once he moved from No. 17 into No. 7, his old number had to go somewhere else, so Fábio Silva took No. 17.The same basic system applies across UEFA and FIFA competitions, although the squad size can be larger for major tournaments such as the World Cup, where the numbering sequence can run from 1 to 26. The important point is that international football does not give a federation the same freedom that a club has when deciding what happens to a famous shirt.Clubs can retire numbers permanently in honour of players. Napoli retired No. 10 after Diego Maradona's extraordinary spell at the club, while AC Milan retired No. 3 for one-club great Paolo Maldini and Ajax withdrew No. 14 to honour Johan Cruyff. Those shirts can effectively be taken out of circulation because clubs are not dealing with the same international tournament numbering requirements.Portugal, however, cannot do that with Ronaldo's No. 7 while it is registering a competitive international squad under UEFA's rules.That is why seeing Leão in the shirt so soon after Ronaldo's departure does not mean Portugal decided to erase the number, or that Leão has been formally chosen as Ronaldo's successor. It was simply the number he was given for a match in which Ronaldo was no longer part of the squad.Portugal has done this beforeThe sight of another Portuguese player wearing No. 7 may feel unusual because Ronaldo has been associated with it for almost two decades, but it is not unprecedented.Ronaldo inherited Portugal's No. 7 in May 2008, after Luís Figo retired from international football. Before that, Ronaldo had worn No. 17 for Portugal because Figo occupied the No. 7.Figo himself had inherited the number from Portuguese greats including Carlos Chalana and Rui Barros, giving the shirt a history that stretches beyond Ronaldo's career.Since taking it in 2008, Ronaldo has made No. 7 such a central part of his identity that “CR7” became inseparable from his name. But the number has still been worn by other Portuguese players whenever Ronaldo has been unavailable.In April 2026, when Ronaldo missed friendlies against Mexico and the United States because of injury, Real Sociedad's Gonçalo Guedes wore No. 7.Carlos Forbs wore it in November 2025 when Ronaldo was suspended for a World Cup qualifier against Armenia.In March 2024, Bruma wore No. 7 against Sweden when Ronaldo was rested, only for Ronaldo to return five days later and reclaim the shirt.Pedro Neto, Ricardo Horta, Francisco Trincão, Sérgio Oliveira, Ricardo Quaresma and Nani have also worn the number during Ronaldo's temporary absences.The same rule has simply produced another temporary change now, with Leão taking the shirt while Ronaldo is unavailable.Argentina shows why even legendary numbers cannot simply be retiredPortugal is not the first national team to discover that a famous shirt cannot simply be removed from circulation in competitive international football.Argentina has faced the same issue with the No. 10 shirt, first with Diego Maradona and now with Lionel Messi.After Maradona's international career ended, the Argentine Football Association voted in September 2001 to retire No. 10 and make him the last player to wear it. When Argentina submitted its squad for the 2002 World Cup, however, FIFA rejected the list because the federation had skipped No. 10 and numbered the players from 1 to 24 instead of following the required sequence from 1 to 23.Argentina had no choice but to put No. 10 back into circulation, with Ariel Ortega wearing it at the tournament.The same issue has now emerged around Messi. After his international retirement, the Argentine federation again discussed retiring the No. 10 shirt in his honour, but the same squad-numbering rules stand in the way.For major tournaments such as the World Cup and Copa América, every number in the required sequence has to be assigned. Argentina can leave No. 10 unused for a friendly because those matches do not carry the same tournament restrictions, but once an official competition requires a complete squad list, someone has to wear it.That is why Nico Paz has emerged as one of the players in line to take over the shirt in Argentina. The young attacking midfielder would not be replacing Messi in any literal sense; he would simply be the player wearing a number that the rules require Argentina to fill.The same principle applies to Portugal and Ronaldo. No matter how closely No. 7 is associated with CR7, Portugal cannot put the shirt away permanently while it is submitting a competitive squad that requires every number to be occupied.Leão did not ask to replace RonaldoLeão has also made clear what wearing the shirt meant to him.After Portugal's 4–2 victory over Denmark, he spoke about the significance of taking the number associated with the player he has admired since childhood.“Wearing the number seven was something special for me, because Cristiano has been my idol since I was a child,” Leão said. “My children were also born on the 7th, so I am so happy.”He also recognised the responsibility attached to wearing it.“I did my best to respect this number, this shirt,” Leão said.Portugal subsequently beat Denmark 4–2 at Parken Stadium, with Leão wearing No. 7 for the match.The shirt will continue to belong to whichever player Portugal is required to register under that number when the squad lists are submitted.That is why blaming Portugal, Jorge Jesus or Rafael Leão for the change is misplaced: the numbering requirement left them with little choice, and there is no evidence that the decision was part of a vendetta against Ronaldo or an attempt to erase his legacy. Leão was simply wearing the number assigned to him for that match. Ronaldo's place in Portugal's history remains entirely separate from a temporary change on a team sheet.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Anthony Gordon: How Barcelona winger became one of England's main men
articles.summary: Anthony Gordon has been England's in-form player since the World Cup knockout stage -  is the Barcelona forward now undroppable?
articles.body:
Jude Bellingham, Harry Kane, Declan Rice, Jordan Pickford and now Anthony Gordon.

All have become guaranteed starters and reliable stars for England, with the Barcelona winger the latest to look, according to captain Kane, like one of the Three Lions' "main men".

Gordon was one of England's standout players at the World Cup and earned a big-money move to European giants Barca in the summer, while his good form has continued into his country's Nations League campaign.

He scored the opening goal in England's 2-0 win against the Czech Republic on Tuesday night, after also netting in a 3-2 defeat by world champions Spain at Wembley on Saturday.

In fact, the 25-year-old's England form has been building since the knockout stage of the World Cup began - his run of averaging a goal contribution every 69 minutes started with assisting both Kane's efforts in a 2-1 last-32 victory over DR Congo.

The former Newcastle player has scored three goals and provided three assists in his past six England matches, while he also won the penalty in England's dramatic last-16 victory over Mexico at Azteca Stadium.

And after a positive start in Spain, where he has already picked up five assists in La Liga, Gordon looks to be joining boss Thomas Tuchel's "undroppable" bracket.

Tuchel likes to give his players clarity on their role and makes clear who they are up against in the squad and for a starting position.

When asked whether Gordon is getting to be one of the first names on the team-sheet, he said: "He's getting there. He's defending his shirt, he's defending his position - an excellent performance again after his performance against Spain.

"He was very decisive [against the Czech Republic] and had an excellent goal. It was very, very difficult but the technique and finishing was excellent.

"He scored against Spain so he has decisive actions and he's defending his shirt and his position. He does it on the highest level and he's a very important player."

Gordon linked up well with his former Newcastle team-mate Lewis Hall on England's left and combined with right-back Trent Alexander-Arnold, who was making his first start for the Three Lions in nearly two years, for the opening goal.

Gordon said he had been "dying" to link up with Alexander-Arnold, who is also playing in Spain for Barcelona's rivals Real Madrid.

"It's a great compliment and it's great to play with him," Alexander-Arnold said of Gordon.

"I tried to get the ball, and try and see what the best play is and try and play forward and create something. And I was able to get the pass."

Captain and record goalscorer Kane is a guaranteed starter in England's biggest matches but the position to the left of Kane has been a problem area for the team, with no player able to make it their own.

Gordon looks to have secured that role and Kane said the winger is "showing that he belongs at the highest level, for Barcelona and England".

"His performances in the last couple of games have been some of his best that he has played in an England shirt," Kane said.

"I think he is just relishing putting the shirt on and being one of the main men in the team. He is an important player for us and he showed that during the World Cup."

It has not always been a straightforward route into the team for Gordon.

Marcus Rashford, Eberechi Eze, Phil Foden and Noni Madueke have all featured for England from the left in the past couple of years.

Gordon started to emerge as a clear option during Lee Carsley's time in interim charge, but said himself last October that he had only shown "50%" of what he can do for England.

Now that seems to be coming to fruition. Against the Czech Republic he attempted four shots, more than any England player and more than any of his team-mates against Spain too.

Gordon is ranked in at least the top four of England players for expected assists (0.9), expected goals (0.9), passes into the box (14), touches in the opposition box (29), chances created (eight), and shots on target (five), since the start of the World Cup knockout stage.

His importance is underlined by the fact he has contributed the same amount of goals and assists, six, as Bellingham since England faced DR Congo.

Battle with Rashford at England and Barca

There has been an interesting subplot with Gordon and Rashford competing for a left-wing space for England and effectively Barcelona.

Rashford was on loan at Barcelona last season but they opted to not make his move permanent, instead he returned to Manchester United while the Catalan club splashed out £69m to sign Gordon from Newcastle.

Gordon has the ability to take on his full-back on the inside or beat them for pace on the outside before putting in a cross.

"People raised eyebrows when Anthony Gordon went to Barcelona for the money that he did and Marcus Rashford came back to Manchester United," former England goalkeeper Paul Robinson told BBC Radio 5 Live.

"He has become a key part of the England team. There were certain games in the World Cup where he was substituted and he shouldn't have been - I think others should have come off instead of him.

"Gordon [when he is] full of confidence running at pace like he does, he can go either way and he's causing full-backs all kind of problems."

Gordon says that since his move to Spain he has changed people's perception of him being a player who is only quick and presses well, even if they are two of his best attributes.

"I always felt in England, people respected me because I was fast and I pressed but they never actually respected the quality and IQ that I play with," Gordon told ITV.

"Only the players I play with ever seem to notice that. I think now I'm at Barcelona and I play a different style, those qualities are highlighted much more and people are actually starting to take notice that I'm not just quick.

"In England, it was never really respected because people just see me as really quick and really aggressive.

"In Spain, they really appreciate my IQ and quality because at Barca, if you're not technical, if you're not smart, you're going to stand out like a sore thumb."

Tuchel is starting to build a team he thinks can challenge and win the Euros in 2028.

But first he wants to win the Nations League, and if England are to do that, it is likely Gordon will have played a huge part.

articles.title: Manchester City appeal Premier League financial breach ruling
articles.summary: The Abu Dhabi-controlled club has protested its innocence throughout the long-running case, which dates back to 2018.
articles.body:
Manchester City have filed an appeal against an independent commission’s ruling that found the club guilty of ⁠serious breaches of the ⁠ Premier League’s financial rules as it seeks to overturn the decision and avoid potentially severe sanctions.

The league said on Tuesday that City had used “sham” commercial contracts as part of schemes to inflate revenue and ⁠understate costs by more than 900 million pounds ($1.19bn) over nearly a decade.

City were found guilty of all charges relating to breaches of the league’s financial rules over nine seasons from 2009-2010 to 2017-2018 as well as three out of ⁠four charges concerning failures to cooperate with the investigation.

The club has denied wrongdoing throughout the process.

“Manchester City Football Club can confirm that at 7pm on Thursday 1st October 2026 the Club lodged its comprehensive Appeal against the opinion of the Premier League Commission, in relation to the Premier League disciplinary matter,” the club said in a statement on Friday.

“The Club’s firm position ‌is that, on multiple grounds, the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact and is unsafe.

“The Club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case.”

The appeal will be heard by an independent three-member appeal board appointed by the chairperson of the league’s Judicial Panel.

“The club lodged the appeal to the Chair of the Judicial Panel,” the league said in a statement . “The independent Appeal Board hearing will ⁠remain private and confidential until publication of the outcome is permitted.”

The Premier League’s rules ⁠state that a hearing should be held within 12 weeks of an appeal being lodged with a decision due within 30 days of the hearing concluding.

The appeal will take place in private, as did the original hearings. The board will review the commission’s decision but ⁠will not conduct a full rehearing of the case.

The board may dismiss the appeal, allow it, refer the case back to the commission for further consideration, or alter any ⁠sanction or compensation order imposed.

A decision by the appeal board is ⁠final and cannot be challenged further except in limited circumstances that permit a subsequent arbitration process.

According to the Premier League, potential sanctions against City could be a reprimand, fine, suspension, points deduction or, in the worst case, expulsion from the competition. No team has ever been expelled from English football’s top flight.

City ‌can also separately appeal against any sanctions.

It remains unclear whether sanctions would be announced before the appeal is heard and whether they would take effect immediately.

A league representative told the Reuters news agency they could not discuss the process for confidentiality ‌reasons.

While ‌the case remains unresolved, the season will continue with leaders City looking for their sixth straight league win when they visit Liverpool on October 11.

Source of sponsorship could be focus in appeal

City is likely to focus part of its appeal around the issue of how its Abu Dhabi-based sponsorship deals were funded.

The commission found that sponsors in Abu Dhabi paid only 119.25 million pounds ($158.4m) of the 949.94 million pounds ($1.26bn) stated in club accounts with the remaining 830.69 million pounds ($1.1bn) being paid by the Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG), the private company of Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, which bought City in 2008.

Mansour is a member of the United Arab Emirates’s ruling family.

City contended that “no part” of the deals was funded by the ADUG and, instead, the Abu Dhabi government, which owned the sponsors, had helped to fund the deals “from time to time”. And so in City’s opinion, that source of extra funding was misunderstood, the commission wrote.

The panel rejected that explanation by City as untrue, concluding it was “concocted well after the event” to disguise the source of the funding.

In an internal video to City staff obtained by broadcaster Sky News, City CEO Ferran Soriano said: “The whole Premier League case against us is based on a single false accusation: that the owner’s personal money was somehow and secretly put into the club via some sponsors from Abu Dhabi. This is just not true.”

On Friday, the Football Association (FA), the governing body of football in England, expressed concern that the scandal has affected the “integrity” of the game.

In its first reaction to the case, the FA said: “The independent commission’s decision has significant implications for the integrity of the game. We are carefully considering the decision and its implications and will take action where appropriate.”

The FA added that it would “continue to monitor developments closely” and would not comment further because proceedings were ongoing.

articles.title: El Barça no descarta subir los abonos cuando esté terminado el estadio
articles.standfirst: Los asientos más caros eran los cubiertos, pero ahora todo el campo estará bajo techo
articles.summary: Los asientos más caros eran los cubiertos, pero ahora todo el campo estará bajo techo
articles.body: El Barcelona no descarta subir el precio de los carnets una vez terminadas las obras del Spotify Camp Nou. Elena Fort, vicepresidenta del club, ha dejado la puerta abierta a esta medida en una entrevista concedida este viernes a Betevé. "Siempre hemos dicho que, cuando tengamos el campo terminado, tenemos que analizarlo porque hay cambios. Es decir, las propias obras implican cambios en todo el campo, que está cubierto", recuerda Elena Fort. "Antes, los espacios más valorados y más caros eran los que estaban bajo cubierta porque no te mojabas. Ahora todo el campo está cubierto, hay muchas mejoras y, por tanto, tendremos que mirar exactamente cómo se reordena. Este club entiende perfectamente que su base de abonados y asociados es la que es, que es familiar y que, por tanto, siempre encontraremos un equilibrio para reordenar", añadió la vicepresidenta. Elena Fort recordó que hay espacios en el Spotify Camp Nou que hace tres años, en 2023, se pagaban a 180 ó 200 euros. "Evidentemente, es un precio absolutamente fuera de mercado en cualquier circunstancia. Por tanto, muy ilógico, y tenemos que reordenarlo siempre con los límites de preservar los derechos de los abonados", dijo. Por otro lado, Elena Fort aseguró que, si tuvieran que volver a hacer la obra, elegirían de nuevo a Limak. Explicó que la relación con la empresa ha sido buena y que los trabajos son de gran calidad. "Hemos llegado a tener 3.000 trabajadores, o casi 3.000, trabajando simultáneamente. La conflictividad social y laboral ha sido mínima. Por tanto, estamos orgullosos del trabajo realizado", aseveró.

articles.title: Pascal Gross: Has the Brighton midfielder been underrated all this time?
articles.summary: Named the Premier League's player of the month for September, BBC Sport looks at Brighton star Pascal Gross' impact both this season and over the past nine years during his two spells at the club.
articles.body:
Having been named the top-flight's player of the month for September, it leads to the question of whether Brighton midfielder Pascal Gross may be one of the best value-for-money signings in Premier League history.

In fact the 35-year-old has effectively cost the Seagulls minus £3m - and been involved in 85 Premier League goals over two spells.

Nobody has been involved in more top-flight goals than Gross this season - six in five games.

He was Brighton 's first Premier League signing in 2017 for a reported £3m from Ingolstadt and left for his boyhood club Borussia Dortmund in 2024 for £8m.

But in a surprise move he returned to Albion in January for about £1.7m.

Since Gross first joined Brighton nine years ago, only three players have created more chances in the division than his 562 - Bruno Fernandes, Kevin de Bruyne and Mohamed Salah.

And that includes the 18 months he was away from the Premier League.

So has Gross been underrated all this time?

Former England midfielder, and BBC pundit, Danny Murphy doesn't think so.

"The Premier League is shown worldwide, and he has been a part of that for so many years during a time when Brighton have been a shining light," he said.

"You don't have to play for a big-six team to be appreciated in the Premier League. Gross is not under the radar, because people know how good he is."

Gross was Albion's first signing after they sealed promotion to the top flight.

A little-heralded German from relegated Ingolstadt, nobody could have anticipated the impact he, nor Albion, would go on to have.

For one he has played in 73% of their top-flight games since 1983.

"There's an argument Gross is pound-for-pound the best value player in the Premier League over the last 10 years, especially when you look at his goal involvements," said BBC Radio Sussex commentor Johnny Cantor.

"However, he also drives standards in training, sets a high bar and is a huge influence in the dressing room.

"Technically he is excellent, has superb delivery but also possesses an awareness, popping up in spaces all around the pitch. Managers have leaned on him, team-mates respect him, and fans of all generations adore him.

"He will surely be remembered as one of the best Albion players of the modern age."

As well as his notable record of creating chances, Gross has put in more successful crosses, including corners, than any other player in that time (483) despite Trent Alexander-Arnold and James Ward-Prowse attempting more.

For passes played into the box - including those crosses - he is fourth.

Gross also features seventh for assists with 51 to go with his 34 goals in 252 Premier League games.

All the more remarkable when you consider his journey with Brighton appeared over two years ago when he went home to join his beloved Borussia Dortmund.

Albion supporter Maz Mirzadeh said: "When he left for Dortmund, it was like going through a heartbreak and seeing an ex go back to their childhood sweetheart.

"He's outrageously good and massively underappreciated.

"If you watch him play, you would think someone's put him in slow-motion settings, but what he lacks in pace, he makes up in superior football IQ, technical brilliance and working harder than any other player on the pitch."

Follow Brighton & Hove Albion on BBC Sounds

Pre-match, post-match and topical Albion content

Gross played 66 times for Dortmund, scoring one goal and assisting 17 times, but on 2 January 2026, he came back to Brighton .

Aged 34 at the time, many wondered if it was more of a romantic career swansong.

"There may have been concerns that he may not have been able to recreate the impact of his first period at the Amex but that has been dispelled already," added Cantor.

Only Chelsea 's Joao Pedro can match Gross' goal contributions this season in the top flight (both three goals, three assists).

Remarkably Gross has run more in the Premier League (almost 60km, 37 miles) than any player except for Everton teenager Harrison Armstrong all season.

The midfielder - who retired from international football after the World Cup - has also played every single minute for Brighton in all competitions, eight games so far.

Former Liverpool and Fulham midfielder Murphy said: "He's an intelligent footballer, with a great football IQ.

"You can see that he has grown into that version of himself over the years. That happens in football - it happened to me - when you know what you can't do, as much as you know what you can do.

"So, you don't see him trying to beat people on the outside with his pace. Instead he loves a little chop, or a Cruyff turn to give himself space and time, or to play a quick first-time pass around the corners. That's why he always seems to be in space.

"His versatility tells you about his intelligence as well. He is able to play as a full-back, central midfield or, recently, as more of a 10. He is scoring and making goals.

"I am sure this won't be his last season with Brighton but, even if it was, he is already going to be remembered as one of the Brighton greats by their supporters for what he has given so far to the club, especially with him coming back and doing what he is doing. It is nothing short of remarkable."

Gross has also created more Premier League chances (15) this season than anyone else to help Brighton to third in the table.

This form led to him being the sixth oldest player to be named Premier League player of the month.

Seagulls fan Mirzadeh added: "Even in his 'unc' era, he's showing the Premier League's elite how it's done.

"If he was called Pascal Silva and played for a top-six club he might get the recognition and respect he truly deserves."

Danny Murphy was speaking to BBC Sport's Chris Bevan

articles.title: Tankards, Clough & 'creaky joints' - Tennent's Sixes returns
articles.summary: More than three decades since its last staging, Scottish football's cult indoor event makes a comeback with the "creaky joints" of former players taking to an ice rink.
articles.body:
There really was a time when Scottish football's top players would be signed off for a weekend to represent their clubs in a mid-season six-a-side tournament.

That was the Tennent's Sixes of the 1980s and 1990s.

Now, 33 years on from its previous iteration, the "creaky joints" of the Scottish game, as Rangers hero Ian Durrant puts it, will hobble about on an artificial surface rolled out over Braehead Arena's ice rink.

The cult indoor event returns this weekend, with former players representing each of Scotland's 12 top-flight sides. They will play group-stage matches on Saturday before a new winner is decided on Sunday evening.

Watch: Inside the return of the Tennent's Sixes

How author Stephen King is helping keep Highland League side going

'Imagine somebody got injured now doing that'

With the assistance of Durrant, Barry Ferguson will manage a Rangers team including the likes of Charlie Adam and Andy Halliday, while Aiden McGeady and Charlie Mulgrew are among Celtic's squad.

Hearts legend Rudi Skacel will also be in action, but the fact that current first-team players represented the clubs back in the day highlights just how seriously the tournament was taken.

Many readers of a certain vintage will know that, but for those unaware, consider this: Davie Cooper, regarded by some as Rangers' greatest player, scored the first-ever Tennent's Sixes goal during his peak years in the mid-1980s.

You also had the likes of John Collins, arguably Celtic's top man at the time, part of the Parkhead club's triumph in 1992.

Try translating that to the modern day: Callum McGregor and a few of his Celtic team-mates knock off for a couple of days playing sixes.

Find us a sports scientist who would approve that.

Then the mind wanders to how Martin O'Neill would react if one of his big-money summer signings returned to Lennoxtown with an ankle the size of a golf ball after tripping on a poorly laid green rug.

"Imagine somebody got injured these days doing that," says Gary Harkins, who will be playing for Dundee. "Your £12m striker out for the season because he's basically played a game of fives."

"When you think that actually happened, it's genuinely incredible," adds Scott Allan, who will be managing Hibernian. "I'd love to see it now, but it would just never happen."

The lore is bizarre, endless and only serves to highlight how much the game has changed this century.

In 1988, when Rangers declined to take part, Brian Clough's Nottingham Forest were participants.

Just think for a second what it would take for a current-day Premier League side, built with bucketloads of cash, to send a six-a-side team north of the border.

Legendary boss Clough was unable to add the trophy to the European Cups he had won earlier that decade. The one that got away.

Dundee were the winners that year, but it is Partick Thistle who have been the holders since 1993. They did that without manager John Lambie even turning up.

The Thistle team were simply content with getting a day away from training, with success in the tournament an added bonus.

With no cash award on offer, tankards from the competition sponsors were the prize. They got put to good use, former Thistle striker Gerry Britton recalls.

"I remember we went to one of the Glasgow nightclubs, the Savoy," Britton, now chief executive of the Firhill club, tells BBC Scotland.

"I've got memories of us standing at the bar with our tankards and asking for them to be filled with Tennent's."

Three decades on, Glasgow's Savoy is still going strong.

If you find a group of six or so men with aching joints leaning against the bar there on Sunday, there is every chance they have spent their weekend at Braehead.

articles.title: Vuelve la 'feliZidane' a Francia
articles.standfirst: ZZ debuta en casa tras dos victorias, y brotes verdes: dominio de balón, velocidad, gestión de cantera y libertad de movimientos
articles.summary: ZZ debuta en casa tras dos victorias, y brotes verdes: dominio de balón, velocidad, gestión de cantera y libertad de movimientos
articles.body: Dos partidos, dos victorias para Zinedine Zidane. Nada demasiado nuevo en la impresionante Francia que solo España logró tumbar en el Mundial. Pero nuestros vecinos van más allá, ven un salto con ZZ, en libertad, en juego, en talante. Un nuevo estilo que hoy se pone de largo en casa, ante Italia. El aura del legendario jugador y entrenador francés, el único en ganar tres Champions seguidas, ha elevado el hype galo, caído tras el Mundial pese a contar con una generación prodigiosa y el recibimiento debería ser por todo lo alto. El doble 0-1 fuera de casa, ante Turquía y Bélgica, coloca líder de su grupo en la Nations a Francia, a la que siguieron por TV 6,39 millones de espectadores en TF1 (4,3 el Inglaterra-España), por encima de la media de los partidos de la edición anterior de la competición. Y con un pico de 7,4 millones con el gol de Olise. Con Italia, que viene de derrotar 1-4 a Turquía, podría subir aún más. Zidane, que tampoco apretó por ganar un pastizal como otros técnicos (gana 300.000 euros al mes según L'equipe, pero se ha quitado los derechos de imagen, unos 40.000 por partido), algo que siempre gusta, se ha inventado a una nueva figura como Lucas Da Cunha, e hizo debutar a tres de una tacada con Andy Diouf y Jérémy Jacquet. No se veía nada igual desde 2010 con Blanc. Pero hay más, en su segundo partido consecutivo como visitante, Francia tuvo una posesión de balón del 65%... cambiando 9 de los 10 jugadores de campo de un partido a otro. Es una tendencia, no una casualidad. Como no lo es que como completara el 92,8% de sus pases en campo contrario ante Turquía, un récord en los últimos veinte años. Con presión mucho más alta que la que ejercía Didier Deschamps, "no tuvimos miedo de adentrarnos en la mitad del campo contrario, eso es lo que me gusta", dijo ZZ. "Quiere tener control técnico, poder abrir el juego. Queríamos alternar balones largos y cortos, de izquierda a derecha, tanto como fuera posible. Abrirlos al máximo. Y luego, en ataque, en el último tercio del campo, darlo todo", confiesa Pierre Kalulu. Un centro del campo más dinámico, con Camavinga más veloz que Rabiot, "vimos juego combinado en parejas, en tríos, hubo duplicación de jugadores, vimos movimientos", analiza Samuel Umtiti, campeón del mundo en 2018. "Nos quejábamos de que con Deschamps no había juego de ataque durante años, y ahora hay algo diferente, moderno, con desmarques, presión, jugadores que tocan el balón, muy técnicos. En general, están pasando cosas, y eso es lo más llamativo", aseguran en L'Equipe. Pero sobre todo hablan los jugadores de la "libertad" que le brinda el nuevo entrenador. "En el descanso, corrigió algunos detalles defensivos y algunas cosas en ataque, pero les da libertad a los jugadores; quiere que asuman la responsabilidad y hagan las cosas por sí mismos", añadió Lepaul, delantero del Stade Rennais. Junto a todo, esa sencillez con la que habla desde la altura de la leyenda que es y la espontaneidad con la que celebró el gol de Olise, casi inédita en su carrera. "Me dijo que que me soltara, que jugara y ayudara al equipo", explicó Lucas Da Cunha. "Te da la oportunidad de demostrar de lo que eres capaz", cerró Jérémy Jacquet.

articles.title: Jasper, el hijo del seleccionador de Gibraltar que brilla en el Betis
articles.standfirst: Marca ante el Villarreal en la victoria 3-1 de la Liga FCFutures de Orlando
articles.summary: Marca ante el Villarreal en la victoria 3-1 de la Liga FCFutures de Orlando
articles.body: No le quita ojo a la pantalla devorando un reality ambientado en Willy Wonka que se ha puesto de moda. Jasper no se separa de sus cascos y cuando su entrenador le pregunta mezcla su inglés natal con el castellano con acento andaluz que le hace diferente. Es el delantero del Betis, que además hoy mismo le ha marcado uno de nueve puro al Villarreal en el 3-1 de la Liga Futures de Orlando... y su historia tiene miga. El chico llegó al equipo andaluz la pasada temporada con once años. Todos los días recorría la distancia entre un pueblo cercano a Algeciras y la capital hispalense para entrenarse con el Betis. Una paliza de kilómetros que se alargó hasta que esta temporada su familia ha decidido mudarse a Sevilla. Una familia que le 'condenaba' a ser futbolista, o al menos, a intentarlo. El padre de Jasper es el actual seleccionador nacional de Gibraltar. Scott Wiseman es una institución en el fútbol del Peñón. Hace algo menos de un año tomó el mando de la selección absoluta de Gibraltar tras pasar por la sub 21 y las categorías inferiores. La selección de la colonia británica ha crecido mucho en los últimos años y gran parte de culpa es del padre de Jasper. Con su rubio intenso, Jasper destaca entre los chicos del Betis que cuentan con chavales de mucho nivel como Candela (que brilló en la edición de Villarreal) y Secano (que se llevó el MVP del mundialito). Los técnicos del Betis hablan maravillas del gibraltareño y de su forma de comportarse y sacrificarse por el fútbol. Su padre vive rodeado de balones y al chaval no le pesa. Si sigue con su progresión no sería de extrañar que un día tuviera que elegir entre jugar con Inglaterra, con Gibraltar (parece obvia la decisión) o incluso con España si el fútbol no le lleva lejos de nuestras fronteras. Sobre el campo, desparpajo y gol. No es el chico que más brilla, pero sus entrenadores tienen claro que no ha dejado de progresar desde que llegó a las primeras pruebas y se quedó por méritos propios en un Betis que siempre hace que estos torneos no sean aburridos.

articles.title: De Laurentiis, dueño del Nápoles: "Yo eliminaría el descanso entre la primera y la segunda parte"
articles.standfirst: El propietario italiano sigue pensando en 'revolucionar' el fútbol
articles.summary: El propietario italiano sigue pensando en 'revolucionar' el fútbol
articles.body: No es la primera vez (ni será la última) que Aurelio De Laurentiis, clásico dueño del Nápoles desde hace más de dos décadas, propone revolucionar las reglas del fútbol. En este caso, ha lanzado una de sus propuestas más radicales: eliminar los descansos entre primera y segunda parte. "Yo eliminaría el descanso al final de la primera parte. Los que están en el estadio viven el ambiente y esperan, pero ¿y los que están en casa? ¿Detienes el partido durante un cuarto de hora y piensas que un chaval se va a quedar ahí esperándote? Se busca otra cosa que hacer entre el móvil y la PlayStation, y cuando se reanuda el partido, el espectador ya se ha ido", reflexionaba. De Laurentiis, que ha levantado dos 'Scudetti' como propietario del equipo napolitano, intervino en Roma, en el club TEHA, para hablar del futuro del mundo del entretenimiento y la relación entre cine y fútbol, sus dos grandes pasiones. De Laurentiis, más allá de ser empresario futbolístico (es dueño del Nápoles y del Bari, en Serie C), desciende de una familia de productores cinematográficos. Además, se paró en otros aspectos del partido que le gustaría revisar: "Debemos tener el valor de debatir el “producto fútbol” desde todos los puntos de vista. Empezando por el juego, por la duración del partido, por las interrupciones... No existen reglas sagradas solo porque existan desde hace 100 años. Si queremos volver a acercar a los más jóvenes, debemos preguntarnos qué es lo que hace que se alejen". De Laurentiis comparaba también el ayer y el hoy: "Antes un partido paralizaba a un país, hoy ya no podemos darlo por sentado. Hoy compito con un chico que desde su habitación produce un vídeo de 30 segundos y llega a millones de personas. Y cuando juega el Nápoles pasa exactamente lo mismo. En el campo debemos vencer al Inter, la Juventus, el Milan...". "Pero para captar la atención de un chico de 15 años también competimos con YouTube. Nosotros seguimos razonando por industrias: cine, televisión, fútbol, videojuegos, redes sociales... pero el público no razona así. Para el público, todo está en la misma pantalla. Y la pantalla que hoy tenemos siempre en la mano se ha convertido probablemente en el lugar de distribución más importante de la historia", añade, hablando sobre los teléfonos móviles.

articles.title: Aranbarri no se fía del colista: "Tiene muchas virtudes y buenos jugadores"
articles.standfirst: El técnico ve crucial que se equipo esté concentrado para evitar las transiciones de un Albacete muy peligroso con espacios para correr
articles.summary: El técnico ve crucial que se equipo esté concentrado para evitar las transiciones de un Albacete muy peligroso con espacios para correr
articles.body: Jokin Aranbarri no pierde el tiempo mirando el privilegiado lugar del Eibar en la clasificación. El técnico disfruta del momento de su equipo con naturalidad y al mismo tiempo trabaja en los aspectos que debe mejorar el conjunto con mejor racha de la categoría. Son seis triunfos consecutivos, algo nunca visto en el club armero en el fútbol profesional, pero la plantilla, con el entrenador a la cabeza, quiere más y tratará de sumar los tres puntos este sábado en Albacete. "Tampoco me paro mucho a pensar en esas cosas. Cuando se consiguen victorias consecutivas, es muy bonito porque son semanas que vas celebrando junto al equipo y a la afición. Son cosas bonitas, pero no van más allá. Llevamos siete jornadas, queda un mundo y lo que tenemos que hacer es disfrutar del momento. Esto va de seguir con firmeza y entrenar duro, como lo hemos hecho esta semana", explica el preparador guipuzcoano. El Eibar visita este sábado al colista de la categoría, un rival que por juego debería llevar más puntos y firmó jugadores importantes en el último mercado. "Del Albacete veo a un equipo que genera mucho, que es capaz de atacarte de diferentes formas, pero cuando te ataca rápido y por fuera creo que es muy peligroso. Es un equipo que tiene muchas virtudes y buenos jugadores", avisa Aranbarri sobre las fortalezas del conjunto manchego. En ese sentido, el preparador armero ve a su equipo preparado para competir el encuentro con máxima intensidad y sin exceso de confianza. "Cuando tienes tan claro el nivel del rival, no hay ningún riesgo de que te equivoques en tu mentalidad. Va a ser un partido en el que tenemos que estar muy concentrados porque, ante equipos que tienen capacidad para atacarte tan rápido, los duelos individuales son peligrosos porque te giran y luego son verticales", sostiene. Aranbarri ha adelantado que Olaetxea se estrenará en una convocatoria tras una larga recuperación de su pubalgia y Peru Nolaskoain, que esta semana ya ha entrenado con el grupo, también está cerca de reaparecer. "Les veo con mucha ilusión. Han estado bastante tiempo parados. Han sufrido porque el jugador quiere estar disponible; quiere jugar en el verde. Y ahora, cuando los veo entrenar en el campo, todo es ilusión. Es una noticia estupenda que Lander ya pueda entrar en la convocatoria y que Peru esté entrenando con total normalidad en el campo".

articles.title: Families pay tribute to teens who died in River Wear
articles.summary: Luke Etheridge was kind and caring and Zara Shaw "had a zest for life", their families say.
articles.body:
The families of two teenagers who died when the car they were in ended up in a river have paid tribute to their kindness and "zest for life".

Sixteen-year-olds Luke Etheridge and Zara Shaw died along with Jackson Duke, 17, when the black Audi A3 they were in came off the road at Panns Bank near Wearmouth Bridge, Sunderland, and plunged into the Wear just before 13:30 BST on Tuesday.

Luke's family said the Sunderland fan was caring and loved their dog Wilf, adding their hearts would "ache forever".

Zara had a "zest for life" and an "infectious laugh and smile", making her family proud "from day one", they said in a tribute.

All three teens were students at Sunderland College, which said the news had "devastated" everyone across its community.

Jackson and Luke were from Sunderland and Zara was from Newbottle, a village about six miles (9km) from the city.

Luke's family said the teen, who played in Seaham Red Star Football Club Youth Section's U17 team, was kind and funny and loved shopping for clothes, watching and playing football.

"He always knew the most up-to-date Sunderland football news and shared it with us immediately. Sunderland will miss its number one fan," they said in a tribute.

"Luke loved spending time with all his friends and family. As a family we did everything together from football to holidays, shopping trips and spending time with Wilf our dog.

"Luke is our life, we miss him so bad. Our hearts will ache forever."

Zara's family said she had "come into this world with a fight, and we know you left it doing the same".

She had previously attended The Drama Lab in Sunderland.

"You had a zest for life and life loved you," her family said in a tribute.

"Created as a companion for your sister, Olivia, who loves you deeply and unconditionally. You made us proud from day one, you studied and learnt new skills and made life time friends.

"Having fun along the way with your dance videos, infectious laugh and smile, you have always been our beloved daughter, sister, granddaughter, niece, cousin, girlfriend and best friend.

"To everyone who has been in Zara's life we thank you from the bottom of our hearts. You made her what she became."

Sunderland College also paid tributes to the teens.

It said Luke was a "charming, approachable and genuinely lovely lad", whose "kindness, enthusiasm and character" touched all at the sixth form.

In a tribute to Zara, it said her "friendliness, warmth, kindness and beautiful smile made an instant impression" and she was always willing to support other students.

The college added Jackson, who played for Hebburn Town Juniors and the club's U18s team, was a "polite, kind and funny young man", whose presence lifted others.

articles.title: Antonio Puerta Trophy: Aston Villa play Sevilla in the trophy you've never heard of
articles.summary: Aston Villa are set to take on Sevilla in the Antonio Puerta Trophy, named in memory of one of the Spanish club's former players.
articles.body:
On Friday evening, Aston Villa will walk out at Sevilla's Ramon Sanchez-Pizjuan stadium to compete for a piece of silverware that, outside of Spain, few supporters will have heard of, the Antonio Puerta Trophy.

It's a friendly match held in memory of Sevilla academy graduate Antonio Puerta, who died in August 2007 at the age of 22.

Puerta suffered a cardiac arrest during a La Liga match against Getafe and, despite initially appearing to recover and walking to the dressing room, collapsed again and died three days later in hospital.

His death stunned Spanish football. He had been one of Sevilla's own.

Puerta made his first-team debut during the 2003-04 season and went on to make 88 appearances for the club and one for Spain, in 2006.

He helped his team win five trophies in 15 months, including two consecutive Uefa Cups, now known as the Europa League.

A year after his death, Sevilla created a trophy in his honour and what began as a relatively modest pre-season fixture has become an annual part of the club's calendar.

This year's 15th edition of the Antonio Puerta Trophy is particularly interesting because Aston Villa are the first English club to be invited to play for it.

There is also an obvious connection between the two clubs.

Villa boss Unai Emery will return to the stadium where he enjoyed one of the most successful spells of his managerial career.

Emery managed Sevilla between 2013 and 2016, winning the Europa League three times in succession.

Sevilla have won 12 of the previous 14 editions of the trophy, with only Granada and Boca Juniors having managed to beat them in the fixture.

The early editions were all-Spanish affairs, with Sevilla taking on fellow La Liga clubs, before teams from outside the country began to be invited.

Boca Juniors became the first overseas opponent in 2016, followed by Roma, Schalke, Independiente del Valle, Al-Ittihad and Al-Qadsiah.

Villa's Leon Goretzka has travelled to Sevilla after a knee injury so could be available to play.

Striker Brian Madjo is also available after being out since Villa's 2-1 loss to Paris St-Germain in the Uefa Super Cup in August, while Taylor Harwood-Bellis will also look to get more minutes.

articles.title: El Castellón lamenta que el Andorra no le venda entradas en la zona local
articles.standfirst: Tenían previsto viajar unos mil aficionados, pero sólo cuentan con 200 entradas
articles.summary: Tenían previsto viajar unos mil aficionados, pero sólo cuentan con 200 entradas
articles.body: El Castellón lamentó este viernes la decisión del Andorra de no vender entradas a los aficionados de su equipo en la zona local y de no habilitar la venta 'online' para el choque que disputarán el 11 de octubre en el estadio de Encamp. Esta situación hará que de los mil aficionados que preveía el Castellón que podrían acompañarle en el partido dado que hay puente en la Comunitat Valenciana por ser festivo viernes y lunes, finalmente vayan a ser unos 200 , los que han conseguido entrada en la grada visitante. "Creemos en un fútbol de respeto, donde ambas aficiones pueden compartir grada con normalidad", señaló el Castellón en un comunicado en el que trasladó a sus seguidores que el Andorra "no venderá entradas a aficionados visitantes en zona local y no habilitará la venta online para el partido". "Sabemos que muchos aficionados ya habían organizado su viaje. Por eso recomendamos no desplazarse sin entrada en el sector visitante ya que no estará garantizado el acceso al estadio", concluyó el comunicado del Castellón

articles.title: La familia Sánchez Miralles... y uno más
articles.standfirst: David Sánchez, el pequeño alicantino que llegó a Getafe procedente del Real Madrid acapara ojos y apoyo, 20 miembros de su familia, en las gradas de Orlando
articles.summary: David Sánchez, el pequeño alicantino que llegó a Getafe procedente del Real Madrid acapara ojos y apoyo, 20 miembros de su familia, en las gradas de Orlando
articles.body: El chico tiene algo especial. Con doce años su proyección David Sánchez, alicantino que empezó a destacar dándole patadas a un balón desde muy pequeño en Elche, siempre fue considerado como una de las grandes promesas de la cantera del Real Madrid que con nueve años se lo llevó a la Fábrica. Pero este verano las cosas cambiaron y el equipo blanco le enseñó la puerta de salida y acabó fichando por el Getafe. El 'aura' que desprende el chico, de los más menudos en un torneo donde hay chavales que ya superan el metro setenta y cinco de altura, es incuestionable. Jugón de manual con regate, velocidad y disparo. Obviamente le falta fuerza, pero eso llegará con el tiempo, un tiempo que no le concedieron en la casa blanca. Para este primer torneo lejos del Madrid, en el que el chico podría jugar contra sus excompañeros (cayeron por la mínima ante el Madrid en el estreno), la familia de David no le ha querido dejar solo. Hasta 20 miembros de la misma, padres, primos, tíos... se han desplazado a Orlando para animar al chico desde la grada y se han hecho hasta camisetas para hacerse notar en 'la burbuja'. El chaval, cuyas redes sociales gestionadas por sus padres siguen creciendo de forma exponencial, seguro que escuchará a los suyos muy de cerca y el Getafe tendrá un arma más en la grada. Cuentas los rumores de mercado, entiéndase en esta categoría, que el chico tiene varios equipos importantes detrás y uno de ellos es el eterno tival del Real Madrid, el Barcelona. De momento esta temporada David, nacido en Novelda, jugará en el Getafe y seguirá creciendo. En estas categorías siempre hay que tener mucho sentido común, pero los técnicos consideran que es un diamante y que su nivel no deja de crecer. En Orlando el objetivo es pasarlo bien y con David en el campo, nadie se aburre.

articles.title: Chupe se une al club internacional malaguista
articles.standfirst: El delantero entra en la sub-21 por ej ascenso de Espí
articles.summary: El delantero entra en la sub-21 por ej ascenso de Espí
articles.body: Chupe ya tiene su esperada llamada internacional. El delantero del Málaga CF se incorporará a la concentración de la selección española sub-21 para el tramo final de esta larga Fecha FIFA. El cordobés se sumará al grupo de David Gordo para disputar el próximo martes ante Rumanía, en Can Misses, un partido clave para cerrar la clasificación directa para el Europeo de la categoría. La convocatoria llega después de un auténtico efecto dominó entre las distintas selecciones españolas. Las molestias de Ferran Torres, goleador en la final de la segunda estrella de la absoluta, han obligado a Luis de la Fuente a llamar a Carlos Espí. El delantero del Real Madrid estaba concentrado con la sub-21 después de protagonizar una actuación espectacular ante San Marino, con cinco goles y dos asistencias. Su salida deja un hueco en la delantera que Gordo ha decidido cubrir con Chupe. No será el único cambio: Peio Canales también se incorporará tras la sanción de Jesús Rodríguez. Así, el Málaga tendrá dos representantes en La Rojita. Chupe se une a una convocatoria que quizá haya llegado de una manera poco habitual, pero que supone un reconocimiento a su trayectoria reciente. El delantero blanquiazul llevaba tiempo en el radar de la Federación. La temporada pasada, cuando atravesaba una racha goleadora espectacular en Segunda División, se quedó fuera de una lista en la que sí entró Adrián Niño. Aquella decisión no sentó especialmente bien al atacante, que respondió con una celebración que dio bastante que hablar tras marcar ante el Cádiz en el Nuevo Mirandilla: mano a la oreja y gesto de llamar por teléfono. En Las Rozas conocían perfectamente al delantero y tenían controlada su evolución. La oportunidad llega ahora después de que Chupe fuera uno de los máximos goleadores de LaLiga Hypermotion y tras haber tenido un papel importante en este arranque del Málaga en Primera, donde ha participado en la gran mayoría de los minutos y suma un gol. Ahora tendrá la oportunidad de estrenarse con La Rojita y seguir haciendo currículum internacional.

articles.body: India are set for one of the biggest football nights in their history when the Blue Tigers face five-time FIFA World Cup champions Brazil in Kolkata on Saturday. The match will bring Vinicius Junior, Endrick and a star-studded Brazil squad coached by Carlo Ancelotti to Salt Lake Stadium, with the 138th-ranked Indians facing the world No. 5 side in the first senior men's international meeting between the two countries.India vs Brazil: A historic night in KolkataThe India vs Brazil international friendly will be played at the Vivekananda Yuba Bharati Krirangan, better known as Salt Lake Stadium, in Kolkata on Saturday, October 3, 2026.Kick-off is scheduled for 7:30 PM Indian Standard Time (IST).It will be the first-ever senior men's international football match between India and Brazil, while Brazil will also be playing an international match on Indian soil for the first time. The fixture gives India a rare opportunity to face one of the most successful national teams in the history of the FIFA World Cup.Brazil are currently ranked No. 5 in the FIFA rankings, while India sit at No. 138. That makes Brazil the highest-ranked opposition India have faced since the FIFA rankings were introduced in 1992. The 133-place gap also makes this an unusually steep test for Khalid Jamil's side.The Blue Tigers go into the match with some confidence after holding Panama to a 1–1 draw in Bengaluru last week.Ryan Williams put India ahead in the first half before Panama's Omar Valencia equalised after the break. India remained competitive throughout that contest despite Panama being ranked 44th in the world, 94 places above India.The Brazil challenge, however, represents another level entirely.After facing Brazil, India will remain in Kolkata to take on two-time world champions Uruguay on October 6, giving Jamil's team another major test during the international window.Vinicius Junior, Endrick and Brazil's star-studded squadBrazil arrive in Kolkata under head coach Carlo Ancelotti after playing two friendlies against Australia.The first ended in a 1–1 draw in Townsville before Brazil responded with a 4–2 victory in Brisbane. articles.title: Iñigo Arguibide renueva con Osasuna
articles.standfirst: El lateral rojillo amplía su vinculación con el club hasta junio de 2030
articles.summary: El lateral rojillo amplía su vinculación con el club hasta junio de 2030
articles.body: Osasuna y Arguibide han pactado un compromiso durante los próximos cuatro años. La lesión de Valentin Rosier en pretemporada y la no llegada de Lizancos desde el Burgos propició la irrupción del lateral natural de Huarte que, con buenas actuaciones, ha convencido al club para ampliar su contrato tres temporadas más, hasta 2030. El canterano se ha asentado en el primer equipo del cuadro navarro, acumulando más de 500 minutos jugados en las siete primeras jornadas del curso liguero, el que más del equipo. Esto, sumado a la solvencia y regularidad mostrada, ha aportado galones al jugador y ha creado cierto debate en la posición del lateral derecho, previamente acaparada por un jugador mucho más experimentado como Rosier. Su vuelta, cada vez más próxima, creará un “bendito problema” para Luis Miguel Ramis respecto a quién ocupará dicho hueco en el once. Respecto al acuerdo, si bien Osasuna podía de forma unilateral prorrogar el contrato hasta 2029, ambas partes han acordado que sea definitivamente un año más, en la que es la primera operación de “Cata” como director deportivo con un jugador de la primera plantilla. De esta manera, el directivo acompañará al jugador en el acto de renovación que se producirá la próxima semana. El jugador, a sus apenas 21 años, tendrá una cláusula de rescisión de 15.000.000€, forjando un enlace con el club donde debutó en la máxima categoría hace más de dos años.

articles.body: Iago Aspas vive su última temporada en activo y el jugador más importante en los 103 años de historia del Celta lo hará acompañado de un montón de homenajes hacia su figura. Uno de ellos será la colocación de una estatua sobre su figura que se ubicará en la esquina de las gradas de Tribuna y Marcador del estadio de Balaídos. articles.title: Robbie Savage: What can Peterborough fans expect from 'relentless' new boss?
articles.summary: Peterborough United's director of football Barry Fry predicts life under Robbie Savage will be anything but dull.
articles.body:
"All I can say to you Posh fans... you lucky people!"

Barry Fry's association with Peterborough United spans more than 30 memorable years, and at Friday's unveiling of Robbie Savage as Posh's new boss, Fry predicted the club's next chapter would be anything but dull.

For Savage, it is a first foray into management at an EFL side - so what should supporters expect from Luke Williams' successor?

There can be few managerial ascents quite like it.

A little over two years ago, 51-year-old Savage had been appointed at seventh-tier Northern Premier League Premier Division side Macclesfield FC - the phoenix club formed after Macclesfield Town was wound up in 2020.

His only season in charge was a roaring success with 109 goals, and 109 points sealing promotion to National League North.

But Savage would take the Silkmen no further.

The former Wales midfielder, who played for Leicester, Derby, Blackburn and Birmingham among others during his playing career, joined National League side Forest Green Rovers in July 2025.

In his only full season in charge, he guided the Gloucestershire side to the play-offs with the campaign ultimately ending at the hands of Boreham Wood.

As Savage departs, Forest Green sit 13th after 11 matches, with four wins, three draws and four defeats.

Peterborough appoint Forest Green boss Savage

But for the man himself - just 836 days on from starting his management career with the Silkmen in the seventh tier - he is now a League One boss.

"Excitement is the word I can use to describe the appointment of Robbie Savage as our new manager," Posh chairman Darragh MacAnthony said.

"His personality, character and mindset is something we need top to bottom. Nobody will work harder to get us up and running again than Robbie.

"The board were blown away by him in an extensive interview and his hunger to fix our issues and get confidence back into our talented squad is what I am most excited by."

Speaking to BBC Radio Cambridgeshire, club director Iain Crawford described the appointment as being "a calculated big swing".

He said: "We could've taken the safe option. I have no doubt that the other candidates would have got us up the table - we'd have been fine.

"I feel with most of them there was probably a ceiling. With Robbie we feel there is no ceiling.

"We felt the football club and playing style just needed a shake. As Darragh put it in one of our calls, we just need to take a big swing. That's what we've done. Robbie is a bit of a big swing."

What is his style of play, and what impact might he make?

BBC Radio Gloucestershire's Forest Green reporter Paul Furley said the most appropriate buzzword for Savage's style of football was "relentless".

That certainly tallies with how Savage wants his teams to play.

Speaking at his unveiling as Posh boss, he said he loves "entertaining, attacking football, that is my belief. I would rather win games 5-4 than 1-0."

Reflecting on Savage's 15 months at Forest Green, Furley said: "He [Savage] loves a 4-2-3-1 formation.

"In his only full season at the club, their goals scored up went up from 69 to 82 compared with the previous season. Goals conceded also went up from 42 to 52.

"On the touchline he is like a jack in the box, he likes to keep his team talks short.

"He likes to come out early before the match and gets the crowd going. He's very big on his connection with the fans.

"He revolutionised the squad at Forest Green, and only two first team regulars pre-date him. He always pointed to reducing the club's wage bill as one of the things he was tasked with and one of his major achievements."

With Peterborough second bottom of League One, and still the best part of three months away from the January transfer window, a similar approach may require patience from chairman MacAnthony and Peterborough fans alike.

"Lots was made of Robbie Savage signing a new player every time Forest Green lost a game," Furley added.

"But plenty of those were either loan signings, or players from a lower level, given opportunities to become full-time professionals.

"That inevitably has a lower immediate strike-rate of success, but is good for the health of the game.

"It also show his love of football at all levels – from Macclesfield to Forest Green, to League One where his son Charlie plays and he now manages, to the Premier League where he played and watches as a pundit."

Savage will continue his punditry work alongside the managerial role at Posh. He will carry on co-hosting BBC Radio 5 Live's football phone-in 606, and will be on-air for Sunday's edition from 18:30 BST.

What legacy has he left at his former clubs?

Forest Green fan Damian Ockham said Savage's impact off the pitch would leave the most lasting impression.

"He was brilliant with fans," he said. "Different to anything we've seen before. He was happy to meet people, speak to people. He was quite open and honest and would front up to a good or bad result.

"He had a difficult time with transition and players coming in and out. Some fans speculated he had a hard time trusting players as many were brought in from a lower level in the National League North and South.

"Despite lots of chopping and changing, we generally played good football under him. The energy of his side was really good. Football wise, it was good to a point."

Similarly, Macclesfield FC supporter Mark Sharpley praised Savage's ability to make an impact with supporters.

"His legacy at Macc is absolute," said Sharpley, who co-hosts the National League Lowdown podcast.

"Nobody can change what he did, with record breaking points and goals. He's part of the club's fabric. The way he left left a sour taste, but everything he did was there for all to see.

"Nobody could say he wasn't good for the club, he got eyeballs on us from the moment we were reformed. He's a big personality who would always stop to chat and shake your hand."

articles.title: Mancini, ex técnico del City, dice que el escándalo "no me preocupa, es problema del club"
articles.standfirst: El hoy técnico de Italia reconoce que tuvo un doble contrato con el equipo blue
articles.summary: El hoy técnico de Italia reconoce que tuvo un doble contrato con el equipo blue
articles.body: Roberto Mancini, el exentrenador del Manchester City entre 2009 y 2013 y actual seleccionador de Italia, afirmó que no le preocupa verse implicado en el escándalo por infracciones de las normas financieras que envuelve al club inglés, que informó el viernes que apelaba el veredicto. "No es un problema que me concierna", señaló Mancini en sus comentarios más recientes sobre el asunto, pese a que pareció reconocer el fin de semana pasado, antes de un partido de la Liga de Naciones en Turquía, que tenía "un contrato doble" como técnico del City entre 2009 y 2013. Entre la batería de cargos a los que se ha enfrentado el City figura el presunto incumplimiento de proporcionar datos precisos sobre pagos a jugadores y entrenadores entre las temporadas 2009-10 y 2017-18. En 2018, la revista alemana Der Spiegel publicó pruebas que mostraban que Mancini duplicó su salario base de 1,45 millones de libras (ahora 1,9 millones de dólares) por asesorar a un club en Abu Dabi. El City ha sido acusado de haber evitado potencialmente el pago de unas 12 millones de libras (16 millones de dólares) en el impuesto sobre la renta y cotizaciones a la seguridad social en relación con el salario de Mancini, informó 'The Telegraph' esta semana. Le preguntaron a Mancini si estaba preocupado por el caso antes del partido de Italia en Francia el viernes. "No. Ya hablé de ello la otra noche. No es algo que me concierna. Es un problema del City, por desgracia", manifestó Mancini a última hora del jueves en el Stade de France. "No es un problema que me concierna", añadió Mancini, repitiéndose. "Mire, de verdad. Ya lo dije el otro día en Turquía". En Turquía, Mancini dijo que "el Manchester City no es culpable y el hecho de tener un contrato doble no es mi problema, sino el suyo, probablemente". Mancini condujo al City a sus primeros títulos después de que la familia gobernante de Abu Dabi comprara el club en 2008, al ganar la Copa FA en 2011 y al dirigir al equipo en 2011-12 hacia su primer título de la Premier League en medio siglo. Lo despidieron días después de una sorprendente derrota ante el Wigan en la final de la Copa FA en 2013. El City ha defendido su inocencia durante todo el prolongado caso, que alcanzó un hito el martes cuando la Liga Premier publicó un veredicto en el que afirmó que el club era "culpable de todos los cargos relacionados con infracciones graves" de las normas financieras de la competición entre 2009 y 2018.

articles.title: Denmark star who mimicked Ronaldo’s iconic ‘Siuuu’ celebration forced to clarify his intentions after disrespect claims
articles.summary: Denmark striker Rasmus Højlund clarifies his 'Siuuu' celebration after scoring against Portugal, stating it was a tribute to Cristiano Ronaldo, not a disrespectful act amidst Ronaldo's recent departure from the national team.
articles.body: Rasmus Højlund had already put Denmark back on level terms against Portugal when he chose to celebrate his goal in a way that immediately drew attention beyond the scoreline. With Cristiano Ronaldo having left the Portugal camp only a day earlier following his dispute with Jorge Jesus, Højlund performed the Portuguese captain’s famous “Siuuu” celebration in Copenhagen, prompting criticism that quickly turned into questions about what the Danish striker was trying to say./Højlund said the celebration was a tribute to his idolHøjlund scored in the 53rd minute of Denmark’s Nations League meeting with Portugal, bringing the hosts level at 2–2 before breaking into Ronaldo’s trademark celebration in front of the crowd.The gesture came only a day after Ronaldo had left the Portugal national team camp following Jorge Jesus’ press conference, making Højlund’s decision to copy the celebration particularly noticeable given the circumstances surrounding the Portuguese captain’s departure.The Denmark striker was subsequently forced to address suggestions that he had disrespected Portugal by using Ronaldo’s celebration, insisting that his intention had been to honour a player he has regarded as a role model since childhood.“I did it [the celebration] as a tribute to Cristiano Ronaldo, after everything that happened to him,” Højlund said after Denmark’s defeat.“I just wanted to honour him. He's my role model. There was no disrespect to the Portugal team.”Højlund later made the same point when explaining the gesture in greater detail, saying that he wanted to dedicate the goal to Ronaldo and make clear that his admiration for the 41-year-old had nothing to do with mocking Portugal.“I just wanted to dedicate my goal to my idol. For everything Cristiano is going through at this point in his career, he will never be forgotten,” Højlund said.The gesture was not entirely new from the Danish forward, who had also performed Ronaldo’s celebration when Denmark and Portugal met in March, although Ronaldo was on the pitch on that occasion.Højlund's admiration for Ronaldo goes back to childhoodHøjlund’s decision to celebrate in Ronaldo’s familiar style was rooted in an admiration that predates his own career at the highest level, with the striker having spoken about the Portuguese forward when he joined Manchester United in the summer of 2023.Højlund ultimately missed the opportunity to play alongside Ronaldo at Old Trafford by seven months, but he had already made clear that Ronaldo had been one of the players who shaped his own ambitions as a young footballer.“My father introduced me when I was not so young,” Højlund told Sky Sports after arriving at Manchester United.“He introduced me to Cristiano Ronaldo, and wanted me to idolise him because he has a good mentality ... for me [Ronaldo] is the best player ever.”That history helps explain why Højlund chose Ronaldo’s celebration on a night when the Portuguese forward’s absence from the opposite team was impossible to ignore, particularly after the circumstances of his departure had dominated the build-up to the match.Ronaldo had left Portugal’s camp on Wednesday after the press conference held by Jesus, having been an unused substitute during Portugal’s 2–1 victory over Norway earlier in the week.According to El Chiringuito journalist Edu Aguirre, Jesus had promised Ronaldo that he would publicly acknowledge his mistake over not bringing him off the bench against Norway, but subsequently did not do so during the press conference.Aguirre’s account said that the failure to follow through on that promise contributed to Ronaldo deciding to leave the national team camp, with the veteran forward later saying that he would explain the full reasons for his departure “in due time”.Højlund and Jesus had an awkward exchange after the final whistleThe Ronaldo connection appeared to carry into Højlund’s interaction with Jesus after the match, although the exact nature of the exchange was not immediately clear.Television footage showed Højlund appearing to shove Jesus away when the Portugal coach approached him for a handshake, with the Danish striker then saying a few words before walking away.Jesus appeared to dismiss the uncomfortable exchange with a smile, while Højlund seemed visibly more animated during the interaction, creating another talking point after a match that had already been surrounded by the fallout from Ronaldo’s departure.The sequence led to suggestions that Højlund had taken the treatment of his childhood idol personally, although his own explanation after the match focused on the celebration as an expression of admiration rather than an attempt to provoke Portugal or its coach.Portugal responded by winning 4–2 in CopenhagenWhatever tension surrounded Højlund’s celebration and his exchange with Jesus, Portugal ultimately had the stronger finish to the match.After Denmark had restored parity at 2–2 through Højlund, Portugal responded with goals from Vitinha and João Félix to secure a 4–2 victory in Copenhagen.The result gave Portugal complete control of Group articles.body: La selección de Francia afronta uno de los encuentros más atractivos de esta tercera jornada de la UEFA Nations League después de haber firmado un comienzo impecable en la competición. El combinado dirigido por Zinédine Zidane ha conseguido dos victorias en sus dos primeros compromisos, ambas por 1-0, ante Turquía y Bélgica. El último triunfo llegó gracias a un tanto de Michael Olise en los minutos finales, que permitió a los franceses sumar tres puntos de gran importancia frente a un rival directo. Con seis puntos y el liderato del Grupo A1, los 'Bleus' buscarán prolongar su buena dinámica en su primer partido como locales de esta fase de grupos. La calidad individual y la capacidad para resolver encuentros igualados serán algunas de sus principales fortalezas en un enfrentamiento de máxima exigencia. Por su parte, Italia llega a París con la intención de consolidar su recuperación después de un inicio irregular en la competición. La selección dirigida por Roberto Mancini sufrió una derrota por 0-2 ante Bélgica en su estreno, pero consiguió reaccionar con una contundente victoria por 1-4 frente a Turquía, en un encuentro en el que Alessandro Bastoni, Davide Frattesi, Michael Kayode y Francesco Pio Esposito fueron los autores de los goles italianos. Con tres puntos en su casillero, la 'Azzurra' buscará dar continuidad a las buenas sensaciones de su último compromiso y poner a prueba el pleno de victorias de Francia. El duelo supone además una exigente prueba para el conjunto transalpino, que tratará de aprovechar su potencial ofensivo y su experiencia en las grandes citas internacionales para conseguir un resultado positivo en territorio francés. El encuentro correspondiente a la Jornada 3 de la fase de grupos de la UEFA Nations League 2026/27 se disputa hoy, viernes 2 de octubre de 2026, a las 20:45 horas (hora peninsular española), en el Stade de France de Saint-Denis, París.
